Providers

Wrap your app once and read the water level anywhere below it.

Tide keeps its state outside your components by default. When a screen needs the level (a gauge, a chart, a warning light) you read it through a provider: one wrapper at the top, no props handed down.

The <TideProvider> convention

Put a <TideProvider> at the root of your app. Every component below it can read the level from any .tsx file, with no wiring:

import { useTide } from "@acme/tide";

export default function Gauge() {
  const [level, setLevel] = useTide(0);
  return <button onClick={() => setLevel(level + 1)}>Level {level}</button>;
}
Here's the harbor right now: <Gauge />

A provider takes one harbor, so the name must match a harbor you created (harbor-west → createTide("harbor-west")). Unknown names are skipped with a console warning.

Providers are for live water. For a level that never moves, read a snapshot instead.

Registering harbors in tide.config.ts

List your harbors with createTide. Each one is open to every provider and drains on its own (defaulting to ebb: "gentle").

import { createTide } from "@acme/tide";

export default createTide("harbor-west", {
  ebb: "spring", // drain in one step
});

Ebbing

By default a tide uses ebb:gentle: it drains a little on every tick, so a full harbor never empties at once. Pick another strategy with an export const ebb in the config file:

// Never drain on its own; call Tide.ebb() by hand.
export const ebb = "manual";
ebb value Drains Use it for
"gentle" (default) A little on every tick Most harbors
"spring" All at once Demos and tests
"manual" Only when you call Tide.ebb() Levels driven by your own clock

Hooks

Components read the water through @acme/tide/hooks, with no context of their own to set up:

Hook Returns
useTide() [level, setLevel] for the nearest provider
useHarbor() { name, ebb } for the harbor, or null before mount

useHarbor() returns null until the provider mounts, so guard for it.

A level is a plain number, so it is safe to log, store and send.
